# Our Playwright testing standards at Houseful

By Boyana Staneva

20 November 2023

Multiple teams across the Houseful business use Playwright for frontend test automation. While building out our Playwright frameworks, we are aiming to have code that is easy to read, follow and debug. To help us achieve that, as a team we pulled together to create test standards across our repositories that use Playwright.

Having test standards aligned across repositories provides us with benefits when it comes to readability, usability and barrier to entry. For example:

- Improves reusability - functions / locators / shared steps / other test code can be easily reused.
- Eases reviews - code can be reviewed quicker.
- Quicker onboarding - naming conventions help new starters get onboarded quickly.

Here are the test standards and guidelines we adhere to when creating Playwright tests at Houseful.

### Playwright Guidelines

##### Data Creation in e2e tests

Running end-to-end (e2e) tests is expensive. Consider other options before going down this route.

If you have to make an e2e test:

DO: Each test has its own data creation. Each test has a teardown step.

DO NOT: Rely on existing data. Leave uncleared state after a test.

##### Page Object Model (POM)

Each page should have a corresponding POM file. All interactions via page objects. All assertions in tests.

##### Test Structure - Arrange, Act, Assert

Follow the AAA pattern when structuring tests.

##### Linter

Install eslint-plugin-playwright.

##### Avoid Conditionals

Avoid conditional logic inside test files. Tests should be deterministic.

##### Waiting

Do not use arbitrary waits. Use waitUntil, waitForResponse, or element state waits.

##### Selectors

Prioritise getByRole, getByText, getByTestId.

##### Tagging

Utilise tagging for targeted runs by test type, pipeline stage, or feature.

##### Flaky tests

Resolve as priority. Use test.fixme to skip unresolvable flaky tests.

##### Parallelization and Repeatability

Build tests to run repeatedly without intervention and in parallel.

### Naming Conventions

Variables: camelCase. Booleans: is/has prefix. Page Objects: PascalCase. Locators: descriptive. Functions: verb + context.
